claims.supported: On these fixed first-100 subsets, the optional-gain pool between Q4_K_M and Q8_0 is small; the oracle ceiling bounds any selector over these two arms.
not_supported: That a deployable router achieves any part of the oracle gain.

That these two arms differ in capability: the paired exact McNemar tests are non-significant at n=100 (p >= 0.29) with few discordant pairs, so the comparison is underpowered and establishes neither a difference nor equivalence.
Any cross-model routing or cascade claim: no second-model per-item outputs are recorded in this repository.

limitations: Fixed first-100 items per task, selected by run constraints, not a random sample of each benchmark.
Single host, single greedy decode (temperature 0.0), one run per arm: no technical replicates.
Arms differ in packaging as well as precision (Q4_K_M from unsloth/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF, Q8_0 from Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B-GGUF), so a quant effect and a packaging effect cannot be separated.
Oracle framing is an upper bound computed with hindsight over both arms; it is not a leakage-free predictor.

The source campaign directory is gitignored, so the raw model responses and benchmark prompts are not in the repository. The derived per-item binary rows embedded under `paired_rows` let a fresh clone recompute every reported cell; re-verifying that derivation from the raw outputs still requires the campaign files (input SHA-256s are recorded).

blocked.cross_model_cascade_replay: No per-item outputs for any second model exist under results/campaigns; only llama-bench timing artifacts (no correctness labels) mention other models.
